The user's question is a trick question based on the specific phrasing "highest common ancestor (not LCA)". In standard computer science terminology, "Lowest Common Ancestor" (LCA) refers to the deepest node that is an ancestor of both nodes. Conversely, the "Highest Common Ancestor" (HCA) refers to the ancestor closest to the root. In any tree structure (binary or general), the root is the ancestor of every node in the tree. Therefore, the highest common ancestor of any two nodes in a tree is always the root.
